# Why Archḗ is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *arche*. This is the file on how **Archḗ** replaced it.

Archḗ has no traditional mythology. Its stories are philosophical: the search by Greek thinkers for the first thing, the ruling thing, the thing from which everything else can be understood. Thales of Miletus declared that water (hydōr) is the archē of all things.  Living things need water; land floats on water; water can become solid, liquid, and vaporous.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Archḗ
- **ASCII form:** arche
- **Meaning:** "Beginning, origin, rule"
- **Domain of influence:** Origin, First Principle
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἀρχή
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 29 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἀρχή**. On the evidence, it means "Beginning, origin, rule".

**Archḗ** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *arche* and **Archḗ** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Archḗ** lives at [/sites/arche/](/sites/arche/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/arche/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/arche/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/arche/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Archḗ** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Philosophy, Ethics & Standards** — The origin and first principle; philosophy’s founding word.
- **Startups & Venture Creation** — The beginning itself; the founding moment personified.
- **Architecture & Spatial Design** — Architecture carries her root, and the cornerstone — her emblem — fixes every other stone.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
